analysis.title: EMEA Metals & Mining: Gold rides a Blue Wave that threatens to pull copper under; Stay OW Gold Miners - Fresnillo, AngloGold Top Picks
key_insights: JPM stays Overweight EMEA Gold Miners, citing compelling value, upside to shareholder returns and net cash positions across the subsector. Fresnillo and AngloGold Ashanti remain Top Picks.

JPM is selective on EMEA Base Metals Miners. Overweight on Antofagasta (copper volume growth into 2030E, FCF inflection in 2027/28E), Atalaya (about 100% medium-term copper growth, re-rating potential) and Glencore (improving brownfield copper pipeline, geopolitical hedge from Marketing and Coal exposure).
JPM Commodities Research (Greg Shearer) keeps its medium-term bullish gold view. Gold's post-election rise on lower US rates and energy prices is described as beginning to fortify conviction.

Gold held up as a safe haven during Thursday's equity sell-off and the rise in the VIX. JPM notes futures positioning in gold and silver had lightened significantly as CTAs flipped short over recent weeks, which likely helped.

A gold range-break higher still needs more fundamental support, including a more sustained decline in energy prices. Technically, gold has no clear evidence of a durable bottom until a sustained break above the $4,189-$4,240 short-term resistance zone.

JPM's base case has the Fed under-delivering on hikes versus cumulative market expectations (one more hike in December), opening sustained gold upside above $4,500/oz next year. Further equity weakness could accelerate the drop in expected Fed hikes, provided energy and inflation prints cooperate.

Copper is caught between tight Chinese supply and post-election doubts about the US AI/data centre buildout and refined copper tariffs. China's tightness is slowing copper's decline rather than lifting prices.

JPM expects copper to take its near-term cues from AI and tech. Pressure there keeps a bearish bias, while Chinese tightness, which could persist into year-end, limits the downside. Unfavorable technicals are the main near-term bearish risk.

For 2027, JPM sees a lack of follow-through on US tariffs as a bigger threat to copper than AI. Less metal flowing to the US means more flowing to China, which would ease China's tightness and erode the dislocation premium, challenging JPM's 'high floor' 2027 copper view.
JPM Commodities Research forecasts gold at $4,500/oz in 4Q26, rising to $5,000/oz in 4Q27 (2027 average $4,775). Copper is forecast at $14,800/t in 4Q26 and $14,675/t on average for 2027.
